title: Status-lite timeline and customer consent options
content:
Purpose and audience
This draft is a compact customer-facing status update + post-incident choices note intended for tenants who saw elevated error rates and truncated streaming responses between 2026-08-09 02:12 UTC and 2026-08-09 03:05 UTC. The goal is: 1) give a short timeline; 2) explain root cause at a high level; 3) offer concrete recovery and verification choices customers can opt into; 4) list what we are committing to next. Use for status page update and customer e-mail templates.

Short headline (for status page)
Partial streaming degradation affecting generation responses in EU region — mitigation in progress, options for tenant verification and recovery available.

Impact summary (one paragraph)
Between 02:12–03:05 UTC on 2026-08-09, a subset of requests routed to the EU inference pool experienced increased truncation of streaming responses and sporadic 503 errors for up to ~10% of in-flight sessions. Customers may have seen shorter-than-expected outputs or mid-stream disconnects. No customer data was exfiltrated. Latency for unaffected sessions remained within normal bounds.

Compact timeline (what happened)
- 02:07 UTC: Canary alert for increased stream termination rate on a small shard.
- 02:12 UTC: Automated routing scaled the shard; routing config inadvertently sent a larger fraction of traffic to a partially-updated kernel group.
- 02:12–02:45 UTC: Elevated truncation and 503s detected; SRE throttled new sessions to the shard.
- 02:45 UTC: We triggered graceful rollover to a compatible kernel group (fallback) and rolled a hotfix that restored normal streaming semantics for most traffic.
- 03:05 UTC: Full service-level degradation resolved; normal routing resumed.

Root-cause (customer-facing brief)
A staged kernel upgrade was applied to an inference kernel subgroup. Our routing controller misclassified compatibility for a fraction of traffic which routed sessions to the subgroup before the kernel negotiated full streaming semantics, causing mid-stream truncation and some session failures. This was an operational error in the rollout gating logic combined with an incomplete compatibility flag on one kernel build.

What we did (immediate operator actions)
- Routed affected traffic away from the partially-upgraded kernel group.
- Deployed a rollback/hotfix that re-enabled streaming negotiation checks.
- Throttled new session acceptance to the shard during investigation to limit customer impact.
- Collected session evidence bundles for tenant verification (see "Evidence & verification" below).

Customer choices and next steps (what customers can request)
1) Accept verification kit and opt-in to replay: Customers who believe important sessions were truncated can request a replay of affected calls from our retained request logs. Replays are read-only and will be returned alongside a compact evidence bundle (timestamps, request IDs, model variant used). To request, reply to this notice or open JIRA CS-4321 with subject line "Replay request: <tenant-id>".
2) Manual safe-mode enrollment: If you prefer, we can place your tenant on a temporary safe-mode routing policy that pins traffic to the last-known-good kernel variant for 72 hours. This reduces exposure to future rollout-induced regressions while we finalize rollout gate changes.
3) No action: If you are confident your usage was not materially affected or you prefer no changes, no action required.

Evidence & verification (what customers get with a replay)
- Packaged evidence includes: request id list, timestamps, status codes seen, short extract of truncated outputs (when available), and the model+kernel variant at time of handling.
- Replays will be performed in a rate-limited manner and may be batched. We will not modify inputs; we will run them against the same model family and current kernel variant and provide side-by-side diffs when helpful.

Operator commitments (what Redwood will do next)
- Rollout gate fix: Update routing controller to enforce kernel compatibility checks and add an automated canary hold for streaming semantics (ETA: 5 business days).
- Audit & test: Add regression tests for streaming negotiations to CI, including synthetic session replays (ETA: 10 business days).
- Transparency: For tenants who request it, we will provide a short technical annex with a timeline of internal actions and relevant build identifiers (ETA: 3 business days).
- Credits: For verified material impact (confirmed truncated outputs that caused downstream user impact), we will evaluate usage credits on a case-by-case basis; affected customers will be contacted by Customer Success.

How to request a replay or safe-mode
- Open a ticket with JIRA key CS-4321 and include tenant id + one sentence describing preferred option ("replay" or "safe-mode").
- For enterprise customers with an assigned CSM, reply to your CSM thread and we will handle prioritization.

FAQs (short)
Q: Will replays change my underlying data or model?
A: No. Replays are read-only and used for verification only. They do not change persisted data or model weights.

Q: How long will safe-mode remain in effect?
A: Safe-mode is applied for 72 hours by default; customers can request extensions while tests and rollout fixes complete.

Q: Will my SLA be affected?
A: The incident will be recorded against our service logs and, if eligible, SLA credit assessments will follow our standard process.

Suggested status page excerpt (short)
We experienced a partial streaming degradation in the EU region from 02:12–03:05 UTC on 2026-08-09. Most traffic recovered after routing to a fallback kernel and a hotfix. Customers who saw truncated outputs can request a verification replay or opt into a temporary safe-mode routing policy. For replay requests open JIRA CS-4321.

Internal notes for CS/operators (short)
- Prioritize enterprise tenants that reported user-facing impact.
- Use evidence pack generation script: /ops/tools/evidence-pack (internal) with request IDs captured from router logs.
- Coordinate with SRE for safe-mode toggles; safe-mode is reversible without downtime.

Draft message variants
1) Short status page: (use suggested excerpt above).
2) Customer email (concise): Greetings — we detected partial streaming truncation on 2026-08-09 in the EU pool. We resolved routing and deployed a fix. If you want us to replay affected calls or temporarily pin your traffic to the known-good kernel, reply with your choice or open CS-4321.
3) Enterprise addendum (longer): Include build ids, internal timeline, and a note about credits evaluation.

Approval checklist before sending
- Confirm SRE has exported evidence packs for all reported tenants.
- Confirm legal review is not required for wording (this is a non-data-exfiltration incident).
- Ensure JIRA CS-4321 ticket template exists and is linked in outgoing messages.

Open questions to resolve prior to final publish
- Final wording on the credit policy (point-person: Rajiv).
- Exact scheduling for rollout gate patch release (owner: SRE-release).

End of draft
Notes: Keep phrasing plain-language; avoid low-level kernel internals in public text. This draft is intentionally short to fit status page and customer email channels. For a full postmortem appendix, coordinate with Applied ML and SRE to produce a technical annex that can be attached for customers needing build-level detail.
